text: Math was a Welsh hero or god. The fourth branch of the Mabinogion, the great collection of Welsh myths, bears his name. It tells of king Math of Gwynedd, whose ceremonial footholder Goewin was raped. Much of the story turns on Math's attempts to replace the girl with a virgin applicant. The virgin state kept Math magically safe and obeyed the taboo, or geis, that he never set foot on the ground. The taboo was a common kingly custom. Ireland, the king of Tara could not spend more than eight nights away from home. Math conspired with his nephew Gwydion and helped build an artificial bride, Blodeuwedd, for Lleu Llaw Gyffes. Because his heir was his nephew, not his son, some scholars read the tale as a sign that matriliny, or descent through the mother, ruled ancient Welsh succession.
